M1.reason: Measured overlap is 0.841 to 0.942 in every view, so the outline passes numerically. Visually the claws are thinner and ragged, and the top and below views show the arms at a different angle and reach. The fingers in the front and back-left views look cut short, so parts of the outline are missing.

M2.reason: Measured size: length 38.5 vs 38.3 (0.5% off), height 53.8 vs 52.9 (1.7% off), width 68.4 vs 68.3. All within 10%.

M3.reason: Head, coat, legs, shoes and both arms with claws are present. The claws are fragmentary: the front and back-left views show fewer and shorter digits, with broken pieces where the original has five long fingers each. The back cavity's ribs and tissue are flatter than the original's. Claws are the part that fails.

M4.reason: Measured colour difference is 7.5 on average, under 15, with every view between 6.1 and 8.8. Cream skull, white coat, red blood and dark wounds match in colour and material by eye.

M5.reason: Not a must-have. The blood, grime and cavity detail are present in the right places, but the claws and the back cavity are softer and smeared compared with the original's sharper wear and ribs.

M6.reason: Side by side at game size, the reproduction reads as a close relative of the original, not the original. The claws look broken and sparse and the coat's hem is jagged and shredded. A player would not mistake it for the original.

M7.reason: The front faces the same way in the front and side views. The figure stands upright on its feet at the same origin, and the forward lean of the upper body matches the original's.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks pass with no errors, and 700 triangles is under twice the original's 844. Visually, loose fragments float near the claws in the right and back-left views, and one small piece sits apart from the hand in the top view. That breaks 'nothing floating'.

C1.reason: The motion strip compares the original's walk with the reproduction's walk2handed, so the gaits are not like for like. In the reproduction's frames 10, 13 and 23 the white coat panel drifts off the legs and hangs as a separate slab, and the claws drag and stay stiff. Parts appear to separate, which fails 'nothing comes apart'.
